content:
samir: Follow-up from the RFC — proposing we move from simple node-id tie-breaks to a tiny per-node causal counter (cid) + epoch for demote/handback. keeps the happy path 1 RTT and avoids extra consensus.

liz: short version: how do we prevent a retry from outrunning an earlier attempt?

samir: cid is monotonic per node. we compare tuple (epoch, cid, node-id). retries bump cid, so we can tell which attempt causally comes later. avoids the case where a retry with stale epoch accidentally wins.

ton: sounds like a vector clock-lite. any change in storage/headers?

samir: just add a 12-byte header: epoch(4) + cid(8) or tunable 4+4. handoff/prepare messages carry it. runtime keeps last-seen cid per prefix for diagnostics and GC.

maria: GC semantics? if prefixes are hot we could accumulate entries.

samir: we keep a sliding window: entries expire after epoch advances + 1 minute TTL. default memory cost <100KiB for 10k prefixes.

jen: ops concerns: what alerts? how do we know it's working vs masking a bug?

samir: plan: emit demote_conflict{prefix,loser,winner,epoch} and a histogram of cid_skew (winner_cid - loser_cid). add a trace on conflicts with the two tuples and full handoff trace.

liz: how does this behave under partition healing? if node A was isolated and its cid lagged, could it stomp when rejoining?

samir: recovery rule: on reconnection nodes exchange max_seen_epoch and max_seen_cid per-prefix. rejoiner ratchets its local cid = max(local, observed)+1. if it sees higher epoch it yields until it catches up via fetch/replicate.

ton: tie-breaker caveat: lexicographic (epoch,cid,node-id) gives deterministic outcome but we should still add jittered backoff on retries to reduce pressure.

samir: agreed. correctness via tuple and pragmatic backoff: retry_delay = base + node_id_mod * small_jitter.

maria: testing: add a CI stress job that runs 10k concurrent demote attempts across 50 simulated nodes and asserts a single winner per prefix and no split-ownership windows.

samir: + unit tests for comparisons and a fault-injection test where prepare messages drop 30% of the time.

jen: rollout plan? feature flag? canary?

samir: feature-flagged, default off. 1) enable in canary region with telemetry sampling; 2) if conflicts drop to near-zero and no latency regressions, ramp to all canaries; 3) flip default on.

ops-bot: rollout-event: cid-demote-ff enabled for canary-us-west at 2026-02-20T18:12Z (id: ff_8732).

liz: one more thought: what about long-lived cursors and client-facing handles that expect ownership continuity? any compatibility worry?

samir: we won't change external APIs. this only affects internal demote/evict handshake. long-lived cursors see ownership timestamps as before; if they hit a brief handoff they retry with new owner. we'll document expected transient retries.

ton: add a small note in runtime/README about header format and how to interpret cid_scans in logs.

maria: ok to proceed if you add the CI stress job and the metrics. also add a kill-switch for telemetry flood.

samir: will do PR with tests + docs + metrics + FF. aiming for small PR and follow-up RFC appendix called "CID tie-resolution for demote handoff". thanks all :rocket:
